why: The draft does not transcribe this leaf. On the page, each month runs along a row of day-cells, with a top row of numbers in blue and green ink and a bottom row reading i–xix, but the draft rearranges this into an invented 19-column table that assigns feasts and letters (e.g. "S Edwardi" in January, "S Dunstan", "Vigil/Nat dni" placements) to cells where the image does not show them.

The draft is a modern English sentence about a planning board approving a proposal with hours of operation, which is not this leaf's text; the image shows a two-column handwritten medieval Latin anatomical text (on veins and their branches) in a Gothic book hand with marginal notes.

The draft's Latin fragments ("de", "secundum", "et", "ad", "vel", "qui") and line placeholders are an invention, because the only marks on this leaf are mirror-reversed show-through/offset handwriting from the other side, so this side is blank and has no text of its own to transcribe.

The draft is the text of a different work (an alchemical "Arcanum Hermeticae" with sections XIII–XIV on the philosophers' stone), whereas this leaf is page 4 of "Archæologiæ Philosophicæ", Cap. II, "Conspectus Philosophiæ antiquæ… de Scythis, Celtis, & Æthiopibus", none of which appears in the draft.

The draft is not a usable transcription of this leaf — most of it, especially the right column, is invented pseudo-Latin filler (repeated strings such as "f[u]t[u] et f[u]t[u] et f[u]t[u]") rather than the words on the page, and the heavily abbreviated two-column Gothic hand (a medical text with rubrics "Cura eius" and "De plaga et incisione…") cannot be read reliably enough at this image resolution to replace it with a faithful transcription.

The draft is not this leaf's text — this side of the leaf is blank and carries only mirror-reversed show-through from the other side, which the draft un-mirrored and transcribed (largely as guesswork).
